title: Tare and ages
html_source: “Tare and ages” is an Anglo-Irish euphemism derived from “Tears and wounds” (of Christ). This section includes Synge-like prose, of which this would be an example.

anchor.prefix: ich, it seems, history is to blame. Yes, it is true. I am the murderer of Samuel Childs. And how I am punished! The inferno has no terrors for me. This is the appearance is on me.
anchor.suffix: , what way would I be resting at all, he muttered thickly, and I tramping Dublin this while back with my share of songs and himself after me the like of a soulth or a bullawurrus?
